title: Fidan Accuses Cyprus-Greece-Israel Bloc of Encircling Turkey as Egypt Weighs Joining Mecca Pact
subhead: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, at a joint press conference with his Egyptian counterpart, cast the Athens-Nicosia-Jerusalem alignment as a containment alliance against Ankara while Egypt studies joining the Turkey-Saudi-Pakistan defence pact. Separately, Turkey is cutting Russian oil imports as Black Sea export disruptions bite.

sections.heading: Fidan Frames Eastern Mediterranean as a Two-Bloc Contest
sections.body:
Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, speaking at a joint press conference with Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelati, accused Greece, Cyprus and Israel of forming a security alliance aimed at containing Turkey, according to Cyprus Mail. 'Before we signed our own alliance, Israel, the Greek Cypriot administration and Greece came together and created a security alliance in the Mediterranean,' Fidan said, arguing the goal of that alignment was 'clear' given the geographical positioning of Turkey and Egypt on either side of the Levant.

Fidan contrasted that bloc with the recently announced Turkey-Saudi Arabia-Pakistan defence cooperation, which Ankara presents as a regional arrangement rather than a pact directed against any country. He said the initiative is meant to increase cooperation, let regional states take greater responsibility for their own security, and strengthen deterrence. The remarks echo Fidan's April warning that Greece was pursuing 'extremely dangerous policies' that could 'encircle Turkey in the Eastern Mediterranean'.
sections.whyItMatters: Ankara is now openly framing the Eastern Mediterranean as a contest between the US-backed 3+1 framework (Cyprus-Greece-Israel-US) and its own emerging Mecca Pact bloc, signalling a hardening of Turkey's regional posture.

sections.heading: Egypt Studies Joining the Mecca Pact
sections.body:
Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelati said Cairo is studying the defence agreement signed by Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan from legal and constitutional perspectives before deciding whether to join it, according to Ahram Online. Fidan described Egypt as a 'natural partner' for Turkey and said it was being consulted over possible participation.

Chatham House analysis notes Egypt may yet join the pact but that Cairo is continuing to weigh its options. The pact, which Turkish officials have said is technically equivalent to NATO's Article 5 mutual defence clause, has drawn speculation about its ultimate purpose, with The Hill noting it sends a message to Washington about regional states taking security into their own hands.
sections.whyItMatters: If Egypt joins, the Mecca Pact would link the two largest militaries on the Levant's flanks with Saudi capital and Pakistani nuclear capability — a significant reconfiguration of Middle East security architecture outside US and NATO structures.

sections.heading: Turkey Cuts Russian Oil Imports as Black Sea Disruptions Bite
sections.body:
Turkey reduced its oil purchases from Russian ports in July and is set to cut them further in August after Ukrainian drone attacks disrupted exports from Russia's Black Sea terminals, according to traders and LSEG shipping data cited by Reuters. Russia's Sheskharis terminal at the Black Sea port of Novorossiysk suspended crude loadings on Friday following a drone attack, with one tanker forced to flee into open sea.

The disruptions are reshaping oil routes in the Black Sea, a basin where Turkey is both a major transit hub and a significant buyer of Russian crude. The attacks add to a pattern of Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure that has repeatedly interrupted supply through the region.
sections.whyItMatters: Turkey's reduced intake of Russian crude reflects both supply disruption and Ankara's balancing act — it remains a key buyer of Russian energy even as it deepens defence ties with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan and navigates the US-Iran conflict.

sections.heading: Lebanon-Turkey Ties Deepen
sections.body:
Analysis of the fast-improving Lebanon-Turkey relationship highlights Ankara becoming an important political, economic and security partner for Beirut, according to an MSN-published analysis. The warming ties come as Turkey expands its regional footprint across the Levant and Eastern Mediterranean, complementing its defence cooperation with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan.

The relationship is part of a broader pattern of Turkey rebuilding influence in the Arab Levant after years of strained relations, positioning Ankara as a security and economic interlocutor in a region reshaped by the post-Assad order and the ongoing US-Iran confrontation.
sections.whyItMatters: Turkey's deepening engagement with Lebanon and Egypt signals a deliberate strategy of expanding influence across the Arab Levant, pairing economic and security cooperation with the Mecca Pact's defence framework.

sections.heading: AK Party Marks 25 Years
sections.body:
TRT World published a retrospective marking the AK Party's 25th anniversary, crediting the party with reducing military influence, expanding rights and investing in infrastructure over a quarter-century in power. The anniversary comes as President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's government pursues a PKK peace process and an activist foreign policy across the Middle East and Africa.

The retrospective frames the party's longevity as a story of institutional transformation, though critics point to democratic backsliding and economic strain under the current leadership.
sections.whyItMatters: The anniversary is a moment for Ankara to project continuity and achievement, even as it manages inflation, a fragile peace process and an increasingly contested regional environment.

bottomLine: Ankara is drawing sharper regional lines: Fidan publicly cast the Cyprus-Greece-Israel-US alignment as a containment bloc while Egypt weighs joining the Turkey-Saudi-Pakistan Mecca Pact, which would dramatically expand the pact's weight. At the same time, Black Sea drone attacks are forcing Turkey to cut Russian oil imports, testing its energy balancing act. The through-line is a Turkey asserting itself as the anchor of an alternative regional security order even as it manages the economic and energy costs of a volatile neighbourhood.
sources: Cyprus Mail, Ahram Online, Reuters, Chatham House, The Hill, MSN, TRT World
